newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index falls sharply at open.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index falls sharply at open.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index fell sharply at the open on Friday in line with weakness in overseas equity markets, brokers said.
The Hang Seng Index fell 191 points to 12,861 in the first few minutes of trade after falling 161 points at the open on turnover of HK$323 million.
"It's a bit unsettling what is happening overseas," said Archie Hart, sales director at BZW Securities. "But Hong Kong has been quite resilient compared to other markets."

The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 98.91 points to 6,303.71 on Thursday, with the fall coming in just the last hour of trading on Thursday. The S&P 500 also fell 11.43 points or 1.54 percent to 720.30.

On Friday, Tokyo's Nikkei 225 opened weak and trended weaker, dipping below 20,000 for the first time in three months. The index closed the morning session down 350.57 points, or 1.71 percent, to 20,150.63.
Hang Seng Index futures were also weaker. The December contract fell 275 points to trade at 12,855 and the January contract was down 270 points to 12,920.
"While some of this (fall) may be due to Hong Kong's getting a bit ahead of itself, today's it's tied to the U.S.," said a derivatives trader with a U.S. house.
Properties led the correction followed by the property-related conglomerates in the commercial and industrial sector. Utilities showed the greatest resilience, while H shares were also sold off.
Market leaders showed the biggest net losses.
Sun Hung Kai Properties and Henderson Land both shed HK$2.75 to HK$91.00 and HK$71.75. Cheung Kong was off HK$1.50 to HK66.25.
Hutchison Whampoa, which despite its diversified operations remains heavily weighted in property, fell HK$1.25 to HK$57.00.
Wharf and Swire Pacific were both down HK$1.00 to HK$37.40 to HK$71.25.
